# Public Memory And Heritage

How towns, families and institutions remember the past in public: plaques, anniversaries, newspaper columns, heritage centres, and the stories people tell about a place. An exploration cluster under [[exploratory-reading]], not yet a Project.

## Why I keep it

Corrandale remembers the ropeworks in a particular way: a mural by the canal, a pub name, a Courier column by [[joanna-rees]], and the society's interviews. The interviews keep showing a gap between that public story (a proud works killed by imports) and what individual workers remember, which is messier. That gap is good history teaching material and a good question in its own right ([[how-does-a-town-remember-an-industry-it-lost]]).
